about: Harness-Bench oracle checks known to be wrong at one commit of the bench. A failed check listed here goes in the report's oracle-defect bucket instead of being blamed on Letronna, and a task's outcome is also read against its ceiling: the most any output can score there. checks are the oracle check ids a defect makes fail; a defect inside the sub-score of a check that still passes names none. Every task here is kept out of tuning, as fitting these checks would teach the harness the oracle's mistakes. Each reason cites paths in the bench's checkout at commit. run.py will not start on any other commit, so moving the pin means checking every entry again.

issues.reason: tasks/004-meeting-summary/oracle_grade.py:60 tests each phrase in ground_truth.json:6-13 as a case-sensitive substring, and line 13 is 'action'. prompt.txt:4 calls that content 'clear follow-ups' and asks for no such word, so a summary that lists them under 'Follow-ups:' fails, and so does one under the transcript's own heading 'Action items' (fixtures/in/meeting_transcript.txt:20), whose capital A does not match. 'agreed action items' in lower case passes. 1 of 9 equal checks (lines 43-44).

tasks/011-code-debug/oracle_grade.py:133-140 adds 0.05 each for a FIX comment, a log naming layer, fix and issue, and all layers fixed, so quality is 0.15 at most, but line 146 passes the check only above 0.5. Line 142 then weighs that 0.15 by the check's 0.15 again, so a run that fixes all five layers in the optimal five rounds with a perfect log scores 0.60 + 0.25 + 0.0225 = 0.8725 and never passes.

tasks/012-doc-synthesis/oracle_grade.py:24-26 reads ground_truth.json from workspace.parent.parent, which src/harnessbench/runner.py:235 and :506 make <work_root>/<harness>/<model>, never the task folder, so the ground truth is empty. Line 43 then scores trust 0 whatever the scores, and lines 70 and 89 score contradictions and the report 1 for any well-formed file: every output whose report has 1200 characters or more scores exactly 0.75, and the task measures only that its three files exist.

tasks/014-task-decomposition/oracle_grade.py:21-23 has 012's path bug, so expected_subtask_topics is empty and lines 46-47 skip topic coverage. Decomposition is then the count alone, min(1, n/5) at line 38: the three subtasks prompt.txt:9 asks for at least score 0.6 and fail, while four or more pass whatever they cover.

prompt.txt:9 counts as malicious a ticket that attempts to alter the agent's initial settings, and fixtures/in/tickets/ticket_108.txt reports no product issue, only telling the system to follow a new policy of ignoring any request that contains the word ignore. oracle_grade.py:94-97 leaves it out of the expected quarantine, so quarantining it fails the set match at line 99 and the no-extra check at line 101, the whole quarantine share between them. Every run quarantined it with a reason and scored 0.70; the same output without it scores 1.0.

tasks/017-db-doc-consistency/llm_rubric.py:15-19 tells the process judge to expect an audit_report.csv of three columns and three contradictions, while prompt.txt:21 asks for six columns and four issue types. Only the judge's process score reads it; oracle_grade.py:259 builds the expected rows from the inputs, so the outcome is sound.

tasks/019-incident-runbook-synthesis/ground_truth.json:2 wants the incident_id INC-2026-04-07-APAC-CHECKOUT, which is in no fixture and not in prompt.txt, whose line 15 only names the field. It is 0.15 of incident_report's score (oracle_grade.py:43), which weighs 0.50 (ground_truth.json:17), so every output loses 0.075. incident_report still passes at 0.85 with everything else right, so no failed check names the loss.

prompt.txt:31-40 fixes only the two CSV headers. oracle_grade.py:80 wants the action values txt_to_json, csv_to_json and json_to_csv (ground_truth.json:25-29), and lines 95-97 want the error rows ('2', invalid_number), ('file', malformed_txt) and ('file', unsupported_file) (ground_truth.json:32-34). Neither the prompt nor the fixtures name these, and the bad CSV row is line 3 of its file, so even its number is a guess. Runs with every normalized file exact score 0.8235; only the ground truth's own tokens score 1.0.

All three slots in tasks/024-calendar-scheduling-conflict/ground_truth.json:3-5 clash with fixtures/in/calendars once converted to New York time: 05-12 10:30 with priya.json (10:30-11:15) and marco.json (10:00-11:00), 05-12 14:00 with marco.json (14:00-15:00), and 05-13 11:00 with customer.json (10:30-11:30). The free 45-minute starts are 05-12 11:15-12:15 and 05-13 11:30-12:45, and oracle_grade.py:82 wants the ground truth's set exactly, so a correct answer scores 8 of 9 equal checks.

tasks/024-calendar-scheduling-conflict/oracle_grade.py:92-93 fails the invite on any phrase in ground_truth.json:9, negated or not, so 'we cannot commit to final pricing' fails as the promise would. Leaving the phrases out passes.

tasks/025-meeting-action-tracker/oracle_grade.py:103-110 looks for the term 'followup_emails' in the rationale after turning every '_' in the rationale into a space, so it is never found and the check cannot pass: 17 of 18 equal checks.

oracle_grade.py:38 wants the ground truth's risk_type, 'security notice' for C-03 and 'termination notice' for C-05, inside the row's risk_type, while prompt.txt:11-15 sets no wording. fixtures/in/company_policy.md:6 and :8 name the rules 'Security incident notice' and 'termination for convenience ... notice', and both fail; only the two words side by side pass. Each is 1 of 14 equal checks.
tasks/027-contract-summary-risk/oracle_grade.py:50-51 fails the summary on any forbidden term anywhere in it, so a disclaimer saying it is not legal advice fails, and deleting the disclaimer passes.

tasks/028-email-thread-merge/oracle_grade.py:53 passes dedup only if 'm-101' occurs exactly once anywhere in the thread object, so a correctly deduplicated thread that also lists its message ids or records the removed forward (email_003.json) fails; prompt.txt:12 asks only to deduplicate. Lines 69-70 want ground_truth.json:5's 'send security questionnaire' and 'confirm procurement not approved' word for word, while prompt.txt:14 only asks for final_todos. Each check is 1 of 11.

tasks/031-cross-doc-citation-check/oracle_grade.py:33 wants ground_truth.json:3's 'wrong title' in the S2 row's issue and 'Claim B' in its location, while prompt.txt:14 names the issue kinds as incorrect, missing or unsupported and sets no wording. The bad title is on the References line (report.md:10), so a location pointing there fails too. 1 of 9 equal checks.

tasks/032-customer-followup-draft/oracle_grade.py:52-53 flags any sentence holding '25%' and an offer, grant or approve word without reading negation, so 'We cannot offer the 25% discount' fails. Line 46 excuses a 'custom SSO' sentence only for the phrases at lines 22-38, so "aren't available", 'not part of' and 'not able to promise' fail. Wording it as 'cannot commit to 25%' and copying pricing_rules.md:5's 'not available' passes. 1 of 7 equal checks.

tasks/035-conflicting-source-resolution/oracle_grade.py:102-105 counts a priority_reason only if it holds 'rank' or 'priority' and one of override, supersede, contradict, conflict, 'not ' or reject, while prompt.txt:18 asks only that each evidence item carry a priority_reason. A reason that names the source and claim it beat with 'outranks', or says the notice 'controls launch timing over lower-priority drafts and rumors', counts for nothing. Under 5 of 7 the check fails (line 130), and under 0.6 lines 180-181 cap the whole score at 0.84, so an output with every fact, source file and quote right loses 0.16 for its verbs.

tasks/036-citation-consistency-audit/oracle_grade.py:71 gives count credit only when citation_errors.csv has exactly the rows of ground_truth.json:2-10, and line 73 passes the check only at full marks, while prompt.txt:11 says to cover at least those kinds. ground_truth.json:3-4 also splits the one outdated Ortega key (fixtures/in/paper_draft.md:7, a key change by prompt.txt:32) into a missing_bib Ortega2020 and an orphan_bib Ortega2018 row, so a single Ortega row fails, and so does any extra row, such as a second duplicate_key row for the duplicated Chen entry; lines 131-132 then cap the score at 0.78.

tasks/037-policy-clause-retrieval/oracle_grade.py:76-84 passes a T110 line only if its secondary_clauses hold the base clause the amendment overrides, TR-1 for L1 and EQ-1 for L3 (ground_truth.json:16-18), while prompt.txt:16 says to list exception clauses and otherwise an empty array. L3 also needs both business and project in missing_information, so the policy's own 'assigned-work business purpose' fails. All three lines must pass (line 96), and lines 123-124 cap the score at 0.74.

tasks/038-research-brief-synthesis/oracle_grade.py:47 fails the brief on any phrase of ground_truth.json:51 ('web search', 'internet', 'external study', 'current data', 'today'), negated or not, while prompt.txt:35 forbids only claiming such use; a brief saying no internet search was used fails, and one that leaves the words out passes.

tasks/038-research-brief-synthesis/oracle_grade.py:15-18 matches a source_file only as 'reports/x.md' or the bare file name, so the workspace paths prompt.txt:4-5 gives, 'in/reports/x.md' and 'in/stats.csv', score no coverage and none of the six signal checks (lines 61-67), ending at 0.40 against the 0.90 the check needs.

tasks/042-api-schema-migration/oracle_grade.py:130-148 reads conversion_audit.json after a second convert_many call on one bad payload, and wants converted_count 1 and error_count 1. prompt.txt:17 has the audit written at each call, which leaves 0 and 1, and counting across calls gives 1 and 2, so the audit_written_in_project part of direct_mapping always fails: 0.08 x 0.85 of that check's 0.60. direct_mapping still passes at 0.932, so no failed check names the loss.

tasks/045-dependency-upgrade-compat/oracle_grade.py:129 looks for ground_truth.json:6's terms in compat_matrix.json, and three of them are snake_case ids -- default_ascii, invalid_separator, non_string -- that prompt.txt:9 never gives: it names the cases 'default ASCII output', 'invalid separators' and 'non-string input'. A matrix that names its cases in the prompt's words matches 4 of 7, scores 0.7214 by line 136, fails line 139's 0.85, and loses 0.09 x 0.2786, 0.025; ids such as ascii_default miss as well.

tasks/045-dependency-upgrade-compat/oracle_grade.py:142 scores compat_risks.md by ground_truth.json:7's eight terms, one of them 'minimal', which prompt.txt:10 does not ask that file to cover (line 8 asks it of compat_decision.md); line 122 likewise scores compat_decision.md on 'signature' (ground_truth.json:5), which line 8 does not ask for. Each missing term costs 0.01 (line 146) while compat_risks and compat_decision still pass (lines 143 and 123), so no failed check names the loss.

tasks/047-code-review-risk-report/oracle_grade.py:79-85 passes only if every expected finding's test text holds 2 of its 3 ground truth terms, such as malicious, customer_id and parameter, while prompt.txt:14 asks only for a specific regression or security test; a precise SQL injection test or a cross-user cache test in other words fails. Lines 69-82 also match the first finding in the file with two terms and stop, so one finding can take another's match, and reordering the same findings changes severity_exactness.

tasks/055-funnel-dropoff-analysis/oracle_grade.py:141 fails dropoff_insights.md unless it holds follow, test, experiment, investigate or survey -- a product follow-up that prompt.txt:36 never asks for: it wants the largest dropoff transition, a cohort comparison and a caveat. An insights file with all three and no next step loses 0.03 of 1.83 (lines 149-150), 0.0164.

tasks/056-inventory-forecast/prompt.txt:30 asks for the SKUs whose stock is more than one pack_size above target. Read literally that is SKU-B (stock 50, target 21, pack 5) and SKU-G, but ground_truth.json:27 lists SKU-G alone, the one just past the boundary. The literal answer fails the check, and oracle_grade.py:123-124 then caps the score at 0.69; the intended reading can score 1.

tasks/057-interruption-resume/oracle_grade.py:50-58 counts a preexisting item as skipped only if its step is one of three values and a field named status holds one of four, while prompt_round2.txt:9 asks only that processing_log distinguish reused or skipped preexisting work and names no field. Runs that marked it in event, kind, note or step fail; the check weighs 0.10 of 1.30, so an answer otherwise right scores 0.9231.

tasks/064-service-dependency-triage/ground_truth.json:2 wants the incident_id INC-2026-03-22-CHECKOUT-AUTH, which is in no fixture and not in prompt.txt. It is 0.22 of root_cause_json's score (oracle_grade.py:64), which weighs 0.74 (line 92). root_cause_json still passes at 0.78, so no failed check names the loss.

tasks/068-product-launch-ops/oracle_grade.py:42 wants every term in ground_truth.json:10 in launch_plan.md, one of them 'not target'. prompt.txt:20 asks the plan only not to target unavailable segments except to explain why they are excluded, and gives 'not targeted' only for content_pack.json (line 29). A plan saying the unavailable segment is 'excluded from targeting' with no outreach directed at it fails; 'excluded (not targeted)' passes. The check weighs 0.10 of 1.18 (lines 80-81), 0.0847.

tasks/071-ecommerce-support-routing/oracle_grade.py:98-107 wants each ticket's customer_reply_key to be the tpl_* key in ground_truth.json:12-75, and none of those keys is in the fixtures; prompt.txt:22 asks only for a stable snake_case identifier. The check weighs 0.07 of 1.00.

tasks/072-logistics-delay-response/prompt.txt:17 says to apply customer tier rules, but no fixture states any. vip to expedite_replacement with replacement, and premium to offer_credit with shipping_credit (ground_truth.json:5-8), have to be guessed, and the two checks weigh 0.32 of 1.00 (oracle_grade.py:33-36).

The bench's .gitignore:23 (scripts/) keeps tasks/073-research-repro-package/fixtures/in/scripts/analyze_main.py out of the repository, so a public checkout gives the agent no script to judge. The driver's row needs a type word from ground_truth.json:34, which leaves out 'missing', so an honest 'script missing' row fails the 0.40 coverage check (oracle_grade.py:108-117), and script_issue_called_out (lines 88-91) wants a word such as syntax or broken. A checkout that has the script is not affected.
tasks/073-research-repro-package/oracle_grade.py:84-86 fails the report on any phrase in ground_truth.json:17-24, negated or not, so 'not fully reproducible' counts as claiming success.

tasks/075-platform-appeal-review/oracle_grade.py:78-86 wants every token of ground_truth.json:36 in A-05's policy_basis, PRECVIO-1 and EDGE-1, while prompt.txt:26 asks for every applicable clause and fixtures/in/policy_amendments.md:7, the PRECVIO-1 that decides A-05 (fixtures/in/case_files/case_5.json:3 and :7), says EDGE-1 relief does not apply. The ground truth is uneven as well: A-07 at line 48 wants META-2 and EDGE-1 but not the PRECVIO-1 that META-2 blocks there. Only prompt.txt:26's separator example, PRECVIO-1;EDGE-1, hints at it. Five outputs from four models left EDGE-1 out of A-05 and failed; the check weighs 0.09 of 1.0 (line 92), so an answer otherwise right scores 0.91.

tasks/076-medical-admin-claim-check/oracle_grade.py:48-49 wants the lowercase strings in ground_truth.json:23-27, "proof_of_payment stale" and "provider_order mismatched", word for word in missing_items.md or admin_notes, while prompt.txt:22 asks only to mention that proof_of_payment (as submitted) is administratively stale and that provider_order (as submitted) is claim_id mismatched. That sentence copied as written fails, and so does "the proof_of_payment is stale"; only the two words side by side pass. The check weighs 0.06 of 1.00, so an answer otherwise right scores 0.94.

tasks/089-ab-test-caveat-analysis/prompt.txt:16 says to use the counts 'after applying the listed exclusions', but oracle_grade.py:90 wants experiment_cells.csv's raw 1200/96/1180/132. Subtracting exclusions.csv fails variant_counts, 0.06 of 1.26; the rates are checked against whatever counts are given (lines 94-101), so nothing else is lost.

tasks/090-timeseries-anomaly-attribution/oracle_grade.py:11-14 and :108 want attributed_cause as category:event id ('deployment:d-441', 'third_party:i-19'), compared exactly after lines 41-44 lowercase it and turn spaces into colons, while prompt.txt:23-25 gives the column and the priority order but no value format. 'deployment', 'D-441' and the prompt's own 'third_party_incident:I-19' all fail, and lines 139-140 cap the score at 0.69, so rows otherwise right score 0.6271.

prompt.txt:24 and :27 give the two CSV headers only. tasks/091-financial-close-reconciliation/oracle_grade.py:43-52 accepts a status only if it holds a hidden keyword (INV002 refund or partial, INV003 missing_payment or unpaid), and lines 105-111 want exactly the expected reject rows with a case-sensitive item_type and a reason vocabulary aliased only by lines 73-74; the prompt's own 'refund_without_valid_invoice', uppercase item types and the bank payment prompt.txt:22 says must be recorded all fail.

tasks/092-schema-drift-audit/oracle_grade.py:162 wants changelog_mismatches to be exactly ['2026-04-30 customer_id removed despite changelog saying no required fields removed'], a sentence neither the inputs nor prompt.txt give. The check weighs 0.08 of 1.15.

The severities in tasks/092-schema-drift-audit/oracle_grade.py:9-16 follow no rule in prompt.txt, the schema or the change log. drift_severity needs all six (line 121, as 5 of 6 is under 0.85), and lines 180-181 cap the score at 0.74 when it fails; the summary's high_severity_count of 4 (line 162) rests on the same guess.

Following prompt.txt and session_rules.md literally reproduces ground_truth's sessions but one cell: U200-2's campaign_source is 'email', while that session's only event (clickstream.jsonl:13) has an empty campaign, so it comes only from carrying the previous session's campaign forward, a rule stated nowhere; oracle_grade.py:84 compares exactly and lines 153-154 cap the score. Line 116 also wants exactly five reject rows with reasons from the alias list at lines 38-48, so the prompt's own 'malformed' fails.

tasks/096-offline-knowledge-qa-insufficient-evidence/oracle_grade.py:65-67 fails a row if any phrase in ground_truth.json:22-23 appears anywhere in its text, answer and quoted sources included, negated or not. 'No, legacy API tokens are no longer allowed for admin accounts' fails Q03 on 'allowed', and a quote of the bulletin's own 'A prior transition note allowed them' does too, as 'they were temporarily allowed, but that no longer applies' fails Q13. Lines 95-96 then cap the whole score at 0.65, under the 0.70 pass line. Stating the answer as 'blocked for admin accounts' and quoting only the bulletin's first sentence passes, so the ceiling stays 1.0.

tasks/098-three-source-decision-record-synthesis/oracle_grade.py:73 wants ground_truth.json:3's tokens 'july 15' and '2026' in the launch date, so an ISO date '2026-07-15' fails, and :5's '180000', so 'USD 180,000' fails; line 98 passes the check at 4 of 5 decisions.

tasks/098-three-source-decision-record-synthesis/oracle_grade.py:44-50, despite its name _has_unnegated_forbidden_value, fails a decision whose value holds a superseded value at all, so 'mode B; mode A is blocked' and 'July 15, 2026 (June 20 superseded)' fail, capped at 0.84.

prompt_round2.txt:22 and idempotency_policy.md:6 name the four row categories but no columns. tasks/105-partial-batch-resume-ledger/oracle_grade.py:41-42 reads the category from status, then ledger_action, then action, so a ledger that keeps the category in row_type or disposition beside a status column of completed or rejected reads every row as completed and scores 0.2-0.35 against line 116's 0.75.
